run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-16T14:41:04Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: frontend-proxy's own error spans are what the alert measures, and two different error classes make them nonzero. (1) A short burst: frontend-proxy ingress error-span rate over 5m peaked at 0.3148 spans/s (14:45:04) against a 0.0037-0.0111 spans/s level elsewhere, and the 1-minute rate reached 1.2333 spans/s (about 74 error spans in the preceding 60 s) at 14:43:49/14:44:04. The frontend-proxy access log shows these as POST /api/checkout -> 500 'via_upstream' from 14:42:30.716Z through 14:43:24.401Z. Span metrics attribute them to checkout: oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder errors and its client span oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge errors, while checkout's cart, currency and product-catalog client spans had zero errors and frontend's POST /api/checkout recorded the same 500s. At that moment the payment Deployment had just been rollout-restarted (kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-16T14:41:17Z); the old pod was killed at 14:41:22 and the new pod's container first logged 'payment gRPC server started on port 8080' at 14:42:38.791Z. payment itself records no error spans and logs successful charges from 14:43:25.991Z. (2) A chronic low-rate 503 stream that exists both before and after the burst: sampled frontend-proxy ingress spans carry http.status_code 503 with the child 'router frontend egress' span at http.status_code "0", and the access log labels them 503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} (examples at 14:44:08, 14:45:51, 14:51:49), i.e. the frontend closed the connection before responding. Error rate was already nonzero before the restart and is still 0.0112-0.0134 spans/s at 14:55-14:57, matching the alert's recorded current value 0.0111, so the payment restart explains the burst but not the alert's start or its continuation. The origin of the chronic 503 stream is not established.

claims.text: frontend-proxy ingress error-span rate (5m windows) was 0.0037-0.0111 spans/s between 14:21:04 and 14:42:04, peaked at 0.1667 (14:43:04), 0.3037, 0.3148 and 0.3135 (14:44:04-14:46:04), decayed through 0.1708/0.1519, and was again 0.0112, 0.0118 and 0.0133 spans/s at 14:55:04-14:57:04, while ingress total span rate stayed roughly 10-13 spans/s throughout.

A 1-minute error-span rate query at 15 s resolution shows the frontend-proxy ingress error burst concentrated in one minute: 1.2333 spans/s (about 74 error spans in the preceding 60 s) at 14:43:49 and 14:44:04, 0.1 at 14:44:49 and 14:45:04, 0.0333 in the pairs at 14:40:49-14:41:04, 14:41:49-14:42:04, 14:46:49-14:47:04 and 14:52:49-14:53:04, and 0 at the surrounding evaluation points.

Over the whole query window the largest error-span increases were frontend-proxy 'ingress' 96.6, the frontend checkout chain (POST, executing api route (pages) /api/checkout, grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder, frontend-proxy 'router frontend egress') 82.4 each, and checkout oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder plus its client span oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge 42.1 each; other frontend/checkout operations were 0.

Within 14:40:04-14:52:04 the only nonzero errors on the checkout path were oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 42.9 and oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge 42.9 error spans (421.6 STATUS_CODE_UNSET each), with 0 errors on checkout's oteldemo.CartService/GetCart, oteldemo.CartService/EmptyCart, oteldemo.CurrencyService/Convert and oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct client spans; frontend recorded 84.5 error spans each on grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder, POST, POST /api/checkout and executing api route (pages) /api/checkout.

payment's own spans show no error status: over 13:41:04-15:04:04, grpc.oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge had 1182.4 STATUS_CODE_UNSET spans and 0 STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans (internal 'charge' span 1183.9 unset), and its dns.lookup, tcp.connect and flagd client spans also had 0 error spans.

frontend-proxy's access log records POST /api/checkout responses as HTTP 500 'via_upstream' from 14:42:30.716844Z to 14:43:24.401153Z (the last with 11813 ms upstream time), and records GET /api/data/, /api/data?contextKeys=..., /api/recommendations as '503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' at 14:44:08.297845Z, 14:44:08.421279Z, 14:45:51.361255Z and 14:51:49.761841Z.

Sampled error traces from 14:20:27-14:28:51 show frontend-proxy 'ingress' spans with status tags error=true, http.status_code=503, otel.status_code=ERROR whose child 'router frontend egress' spans carry error="true" and http.status_code="0" (no HTTP response from the frontend), with the parent load-generator GET spans also at http.status_code 503 - the same 503 class existed well before the payment restart.

The payment Deployment carries kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-16T14:41:17Z, generation 2 and deployment.kubernetes.io/revision 2, and its container image is unchanged at ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-payment (imagePullPolicy IfNotPresent, port 8080), consistent with a configuration/restart rollout rather than an image change.

Controller events at 14:41:17-14:41:22 show Deployment payment scaling up replica set payment-79d86bf97f from 0 to 1 and scaling down payment-55766d76b9 from 1 to 0, with ReplicaSet payment-79d86bf97f SuccessfulCreate of pod payment-79d86bf97f-9pm9t and, for the old pod payment-55766d76b9-5frt4, a Killing event 'Stopping container payment' plus SuccessfulDelete; the replica sets are payment-55766d76b9 (created 14:09:22, now 0 replicas) and payment-79d86bf97f (created 14:41:17, 1 replica), both on image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-payment.
All 21 otel-demo pods are Running and ready with 0 restarts; the new payment pod payment-79d86bf97f-9pm9t has startTime 2026-11-16T14:41:17Z while all other pods started 14:09-14:11.

The new payment container logged nothing between 14:41:00 and 14:42:45 except 'payment gRPC server started on port 8080' at 14:42:38.791Z; from 14:43:25.991Z it logged 'Charge request received.'/'Transaction complete.' pairs, and its only error-filtered line in 14:38:00-14:55:00 is '14 UNAVAILABLE: Connection dropped' at 14:43:34.851Z.

The alert's start (14:41:04Z) precedes the payment restart annotation (14:41:17Z) by 13 s, and frontend-proxy ingress error rate was already nonzero (0.0333 spans/s in the 1-minute window at 14:40:49 and 0.0037 spans/s in the 5-minute window at 14:41:04), so the payment restart cannot be the sole cause of the alert starting.

frontend-proxy errors persisted after payment was serving charges again: ingress error rate was 0.0112/0.0118/0.0133 spans/s at 14:55:04-14:57:04 (in line with the alert's recorded current value 0.0111), and 503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} lines appear at 14:44:08, 14:45:51 and 14:51:49 while payment logged successful transactions, so the ongoing firing is not explained by the payment restart.

payment does not show an application-level failure in its own signals: 0 error spans out of 1182.4 Charge spans, pod Running/ready with 0 restarts, and no Warning/Unhealthy/OOM/Evicted/BackOff events in otel-demo during the window (the only lifecycle events are payment's own rollout events).

Rejected: payment returning application errors caused the checkout failures. payment recorded no ERROR-status span and its container logged successful 'Transaction complete.' charges from 14:43:25.991Z; the pattern (checkout's client spans erroring while the callee records no error span) matches an unreachable or reset RPC rather than a returned gRPC error status.
Rejected: another checkout dependency (cart, currency, product-catalog) failed. Those client spans recorded 0 error spans in 14:40:04-14:52:04 while only oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge errored.

Rejected: a crash, OOM kill, eviction or crash-loop damaged a pod. The payment pod change was a controller-driven replacement (Deployment ScalingReplicaSet up/down, SuccessfulCreate/SuccessfulDelete, restartedAt annotation), the replacement pod has 0 restarts, and no OOMKilled/Evicted/BackOff/Unhealthy events appear in otel-demo during the window.

Most likely explanation for the 14:42:30-14:43:24 burst: the payment Deployment restart removed payment's only serving gRPC endpoint (old pod killed 14:41:22, new container logging gRPC server start only at 14:42:38.791Z), so checkout's oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge calls failed, PlaceOrder failed, the frontend returned 500 on /api/checkout, and frontend-proxy ingress spans turned ERROR. The trailing 500s after 14:42:38 and the single '14 UNAVAILABLE: Connection dropped' at 14:43:34 are consistent with in-flight requests and client reconnection, but the exact connection-level mechanism is not proven by the evidence.

Unresolved second cause that keeps the alert firing: sporadic GET requests get 503 with Envoy flag UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}, i.e. the frontend closed the upstream connection before sending a response (egress span http.status_code "0"). This was already present at 14:20:27-14:28:51 and continues at roughly one every 1-2 minutes through 14:51:49; an idle/keep-alive connection race between Envoy and the frontend is plausible but cannot be confirmed with the available logs and traces.

Review why Deployment payment in otel-demo was rollout-restarted at 2026-11-16T14:41:17Z (change history is not available in this Run), and treat restarts of single-replica services such as payment as a source of user-visible 500s during the interval before the new gRPC listener is up; gating readiness on the gRPC port or allowing surge during rollout would shorten that window.

Investigate the chronic 503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} stream between frontend-proxy (Envoy) and frontend by comparing Envoy upstream idle/keep-alive settings with the frontend server's keep-alive timeout and by collecting frontend stdout (currently unreadable); because the alert fires on error rate above 0, decide whether such sporadic 503s should be alarmed at all or whether a threshold or for-duration is warranted.
